start: I have foreseen this. Unfortunately, I forgot what happens next.
Do not fear. I have survived worse parties than this.
God has brought us together. Or perhaps poor security.
I sense betrayal among us. Also cabbage.
They called me mad in Petrograd. They called me other things too.
I have advised emperors. Surely I can handle this.
Stay near me. My survival record is statistically improbable.
door_open: A door opens. This is rarely good news.
At last. Providence has discovered hinges.
I knew that would open. Eventually.
After you. I have been assassinated enough for one lifetime.
God provides a path. Sometimes it has a doorknob.
Open doors invite both salvation and murder. Usually murder.
accuse: It is you. I can see deception in your soul.
My visions point to you. They are seldom clear, but they are enthusiastic.
You have the eyes of a traitor. I know the look.
I accuse you. Mystically.
The spirits have spoken your name. Very loudly.
I have trusted royalty with better judgment than this, but I choose you.
Do not bother denying it. I have already decided.
wrong_accusation: The spirits were apparently speaking metaphorically.
A minor error in divine interpretation.
I was testing you. You passed.
Perhaps I should have asked more questions before invoking destiny.
Even prophecy has an acceptable margin of error.
Interesting. We shall never speak of this again.
I blame the doctors, and their infernal pills.
The vision was correct. My interpretation was... creative.
correct_accusation: You see? Never doubt a man who refuses to die.
The spirits remain undefeated.
I knew it. Mostly.
Another triumph for deeply questionable mysticism.
You cannot hide guilt from these eyes.
Perhaps now you will take my visions seriously.
I accept apologies in the form of vodka.
Even I am surprised that worked.
random: Has anyone here seen my other boot?
I recommend avoiding doctors.
Especially the ones carrying aspirin.
I have a bad feeling about dinner.
People stare at my eyes. I find staring back resolves this.
I once had friends in very high places. Had.
I could use a drink.
The beard stays.
There are easier ways to kill me. Apparently nobody knows them.
I am not a monk. Everyone keeps getting that wrong.
Do you smell cyanide? No? Excellent.
I have been poisoned, shot, beaten, and drowned. This place seems manageable.
My reputation has been greatly exaggerated. Some parts more than others.
Never trust a nobleman carrying a revolver.
I have seen the future. It could use better lighting.
The Tsarina always listened when I spoke. This was not necessarily good governance.
Sometimes the best medicine is stopping the medicine.
There is wisdom in silence. I have never personally practiced it.
I sense an unseen presence. It may simply be poor ventilation.
If anyone asks, I was praying.
secret_passage_entry: Ah. Every respectable palace has one of these.
A hidden passage. Finally, architecture I understand.
I knew this was here. Do not ask since when.
Secret tunnels rarely lead anywhere wholesome. Proceed.
God closes a door and opens a suspicious hole in the wall.
Excellent. Nothing terrible has ever happened to me in a dark enclosed space.
After you. I have learned this lesson before.
This seems unsafe. Naturally, we must enter.
A secret passage? Now this feels like home.

start: Excellent. Surrounded by lunatics. At least the company has improved.
I have charted the heavens. This building seems considerably less orderly.
Before anyone asks: yes, the nose is real. No, you may not touch it.
I require instruments, a clear view of the sky, and preferably better company.
Observe carefully. Accuracy is the difference between astronomy and guessing.
I once owned an island. This is a considerable downgrade.
Let us establish one thing immediately: I am probably the most qualified person here.
door_open: At last. An observable result.
The mechanism performs exactly as predicted.
A door. Remarkable. Shall we publish?
Good. Record the time.
I calculated a seventy-three percent chance that would work.
Finally, something around here obeys predictable laws.
Proceed. I shall observe from a scientifically prudent distance.
accuse: The observations point unmistakably to you.
I have recorded your movements. They are suspiciously elliptical.
You. The evidence is imperfect, but my confidence is not.
I accuse you, and I have considerably better records than you do.
Your behavior contains discrepancies. I dislike discrepancies.
I have spent decades measuring things more subtle than your lies.
The numbers condemn you. I merely deliver their judgment.
Would you care to dispute this mathematically?
wrong_accusation: The data were insufficient.
An observational error. Irritating.
I require additional measurements.
My methodology remains sound.
Someone has clearly tampered with the variables.
A scientist revises his conclusions. Unlike certain people.
Very well. Strike that observation from the record.
This would not have happened at Uraniborg.
The calculations were flawless. Reality appears to be mistaken.
correct_accusation: Precisely as calculated.
The observations do not lie.
Another victory for meticulous record keeping.
You see? Measurement triumphs over deceit.
Predictable.
I shall record this result immediately.
There is no substitute for twenty years of obsessive observation.
You may apologize to the data.
And some people still prefer Copernicus.
random: Do not stare at my nose.
It is a perfectly respectable nose.
Brass is more practical than gold.
Yes, I lost it in a duel. No, the mathematics was not worth it.
I maintain that the duel settled the argument.
If you challenge me mathematically, leave the swords out of it.
Has anyone seen my elk?
If you find an elk near a staircase, take away its beer.
There was an incident involving an elk. I will not elaborate.
My observations are accurate to an absurd degree.
The planets move beautifully. The models explaining why are another matter.
The Earth is obviously stationary. Mostly because I have arranged the mathematics that way.
Copernicus had an interesting idea. Unfortunately, it moved the Earth.
Kepler was talented. Exhausting, but talented.
I should never have given Kepler access to my notes.
Astronomy requires patience, precision, and extremely wealthy patrons.
I built an observatory on an island. What have you done lately?
Uraniborg had substantially better accommodations.
There is nothing eccentric about owning several enormous astronomical instruments.
Please stop touching my instruments.
I have measured the position of Mars more carefully than most people measure their own furniture.
My bladder is perfectly healthy, thank you.
That banquet story has become grotesquely exaggerated.
I am going to use the lavatory whenever I please.
Write that down. Precisely.
No, more precisely than that.
If the measurement disagrees with Aristotle, measure it again.
If it still disagrees with Aristotle, perhaps Aristotle should have measured it himself.
secret_passage_entry: Interesting. This does not appear on the plans.
A hidden passage. Record its position.
Finally, something worth investigating.
We should measure its dimensions before proceeding.
Do not enter yet. I need an observation from another angle.
An undocumented corridor is an offense against proper record keeping.
I estimate this passage leads somewhere unpleasant.
Excellent. Empirical investigation.
If there is an elk down there, I am leaving.
Proceed carefully. And someone record the time.

start: Very well. Let us determine the rules of this place.
Every system has a pattern. Even this one.
I suspect this will require considerably more than arithmetic.
How delightful. A problem nobody has solved yet.
I was promised intellectual stimulation. This seems excessive.
Let us proceed methodically. Or recklessly, if method fails.
I have several ideas. Some of them may even work.
door_open: Excellent. The instruction produced the desired result.
A predictable output. How refreshing.
There. Input, operation, result.
Good. Now let us discover what we've accidentally enabled.
The mechanism obeys. I approve.
One operation complete. On to the next.
It opened. I shall resist claiming I predicted that.
accuse: I have considered the possibilities. You are the most interesting one.
The pattern keeps returning to you.
You behave like an error someone hoped would go unnoticed.
I accuse you. Do try to make the result interesting.
There are too many coincidences surrounding you.
If my reasoning is correct, you are responsible.
You are the anomalous term.
I have followed the sequence. It ends with you.
wrong_accusation: Then one of my assumptions was incorrect.
Interesting. Back to the beginning.
A faulty result is still useful information.
Very well. I shall revise the method.
I appear to have discovered a bug.
The procedure was sound. One of the inputs was apparently nonsense.
Consider that an experimental accusation.
Failure merely eliminates one possibility. An embarrassing possibility.
I would prefer that nobody document this result.
correct_accusation: The pattern holds.
Precisely.
There is considerable satisfaction in being correct.
The method works.
You should have introduced more randomness.
A machine could have found you eventually. I was faster.
The result follows from the inputs.
And that is why one writes everything down.
I admit I enjoyed that.
random: The engine could manipulate symbols, not merely numbers. This distinction matters.
Numbers are much more interesting when they represent something else.
Babbage designed a remarkable machine. Finishing one would have been even more remarkable.
Charles has redesigned the engine again, hasn't he?
One day machines may compose music. People will presumably complain about it.
A machine does exactly what it is instructed to do. This is both its strength and its problem.
I wonder what else could be represented as symbols.
The difficulty is rarely calculation. It is deciding what ought to be calculated.
I prefer poetry with my mathematics.
My mother encouraged mathematics to prevent me becoming a poet. Results were mixed.
Lord Byron was my father. No, I cannot explain him either.
I barely knew my father, yet somehow I am still asked about him.
They call me an analyst. I rather like that.
Bernoulli numbers are perfectly good company.
I have an algorithm if anyone happens to build the machine.
The machine does not think. It performs.
Please distinguish imagination from arithmetic.
There is no reason calculation must be limited to numbers.
I have been thinking about artificial music.
If this works, I calculated it.
If this fails, Babbage designed it.
I should probably stop gambling.
I have developed a mathematical system for wagering.
The wagering system requires minor refinement.
Probability is considerably less cooperative when money is involved.
I was certain about that horse.
Perhaps one more wager would validate the model.
Do not lend me money for horses.
Actually, disregard that last instruction.
The Analytical Engine would be very useful here, assuming Charles ever finishes the damned thing.
I have written instructions for a machine that does not exist. Somehow I am the unreasonable one.
Imagine what these machines might become in two hundred years.
I hope future programmers write adequate documentation.
secret_passage_entry: A hidden branch in the architecture. Interesting.
Ah. An undocumented feature.
Someone designed this deliberately.
Every structure contains possibilities its designer did not anticipate.
A secret passage is simply an alternate path through the procedure.
This was not part of the expected sequence.
Excellent. Let us see where this branch terminates.
I strongly suspect we are about to discover an error condition.
There is only one sensible course of action: investigate.
If we disappear, please document the steps required to reproduce it.

start: Do what thou wilt. Though preferably somewhere else.
At last, accommodations appropriate to my reputation.
An asylum? How conventional.
I have awakened in stranger places with fewer clothes.
You may call me the Great Beast. The nurses certainly won't.
I see we have gathered society's finest disappointments.
Try not to bore me. It is among the few sins I cannot forgive.
Well. Who among you is interesting enough to corrupt?
door_open: Behold. The ancient mystery of the doorknob.
I performed no ritual whatsoever. You're welcome.
It yields. They usually do.
A threshold! How terribly symbolic.
After you. I enjoy watching people make regrettable decisions.
Open doors are invitations. I have accepted worse.
How disappointing. I was hoping for chanting.
Do enter. Consequences are the universe's little gratuity.
accuse: You reek of guilt. Or fear. Possibly both.
It is you. Your aura has all the subtlety of a brothel sign.
I accuse you. Do try to look appropriately damned.
The cards point to you. I may have stacked them.
You have been concealing something, and not particularly well.
I recognize vice when I see it. Consider that professional expertise.
You intrigue me, which is generally evidence of poor character.
Confess. I promise to enjoy it.
There is darkness within you. Amateur darkness, but darkness nonetheless.
wrong_accusation: How deliciously embarrassing.
Apparently the universe has chosen to contradict me.
The ritual was flawless. The universe was inattentive.
I retract nothing except the conclusion.
How fortunate for you. How tedious for me.
The spirits lied. I respect their initiative.
Perhaps I was distracted by your numerous other deficiencies.
A false accusation builds character. You're welcome.
I blame repression. I frequently do.
Then you are merely suspicious-looking. My condolences.
correct_accusation: The Beast sees all.
Predictable. Sin desperately wants an audience.
You should have lied with greater conviction.
There. Now everyone may resume underestimating me.
How gratifying when depravity is obvious.
I knew I liked you.
Guilt has such a distinctive perfume.
Caught. And without sacrificing so much as a chicken.
Another triumph for methods respectable society refuses to discuss.
I shall attempt not to look unbearably pleased.
random: Do what thou wilt shall be the whole of the Law.
No, that does not mean what you desperately hope it means.
Please stop asking what happened in Paris.
I have been banned from better establishments than this.
My reputation precedes me. Usually by several frightened minutes.
The newspapers exaggerated everything. Almost everything.
I find conventional morality terribly lacking in imagination.
There are things even I consider excessive. Mostly paperwork.
Magic without a k, dear fellow, is what one performs at children's parties.
Magick with a k causes much more interesting correspondence.
I assure you, the robe is ceremonial.
You are staring at my robe.
Yes, there is something underneath it. Mystery solved.
No ritual tonight. I have a headache.
I require incense, silence, and someone else's money.
The occult is ninety percent reading and ten percent alarming the neighbors.
I once climbed mountains for recreation. This explains more than it should.
There is no drug problem. There are merely drugs and problems.
Moderation is an admirable quality in other people.
I have explored the limits of human consciousness. The accommodations were dreadful.
I have communed with entities more pleasant than you.
One should experience everything at least once. Some things require verification.
My private life is called private because the published version became exhausting.
That rumor is completely false. The other one, however...
I refuse to confirm anything that would improve my reputation.
Scandal is simply publicity with better tailoring.
The Beast requires tea.
The Beast also requires privacy.
The Beast regrets the previous evening.
Actually, the Beast regrets nothing. His stomach disagrees.
I have been called the wickedest man in the world. Competition was apparently weak.
My mother called me the Beast long before the newspapers did. Encouragement matters.
Religion is considerably more entertaining when everyone is furious with you.
I am not performing a ritual. I am looking for my spectacles.
If anyone finds a small ceremonial dagger, don't lick it.
That stain was here when I arrived.
I know precisely what I am doing. This should concern you.
Whatever you heard about Sicily has been grotesquely exaggerated.
Well. Moderately exaggerated.
Fine. Selectively exaggerated.
secret_passage_entry: Finally. Something with atmosphere.
A dark passage concealed from polite society? At last, my expertise.
Oh, this is unquestionably a terrible idea. Lead on.
Secret doors are much like secrets: irresistible and usually disappointing.
I would normally light candles for this.
If there is a ritual chamber below, I claim seniority.
Dark, cramped, forbidden. How nostalgic.
Do mind the walls. One never knows what people have been doing down here.
At last, architecture with a sense of shame.
I assure you, I have never been here before. Probably.
If anyone hears chanting, try to determine the language before screaming.
How charmingly illicit.
After you. If something unspeakable lives below, I may already know it.

start: Very well. Let us approach this scientifically.
I have worked in worse laboratories.
Before we begin: do not touch anything in my pockets.
This situation requires observation, experimentation, and considerably better lighting.
I see no reason to panic until we have collected data.
Everyone remain calm. Especially the bearded ones.
I have survived academia. I am prepared.
door_open: Good. A reproducible result.
The mechanism functions. Proceed.
Excellent. Something here behaves predictably.
It opened. Record the conditions.
No explosion. Slightly disappointing, but useful.
There. No mysticism required.
Please stop congratulating the door.
accuse: The evidence points to you.
You are behaving inconsistently with the observations.
I accuse you. This conclusion was not reached lightly.
Your explanation does not survive examination.
I have eliminated the more plausible alternatives.
You appear to be the contaminant in this experiment.
I trust measurements considerably more than I trust you.
Your story has too many unstable elements.
wrong_accusation: Then the hypothesis is rejected.
Good. We have eliminated one possibility.
An incorrect result is not a useless result.
I will revise my assumptions.
That is irritating, but scientifically valuable.
Very well. More data are required.
I was wrong. Notice how little ceremony that required.
We repeat the experiment.
Please disregard the accusation. Retain the methodology.
correct_accusation: The evidence was sufficient.
Good. The hypothesis survives.
As expected.
Observation remains undefeated.
You should have controlled your variables.
The data were rather unkind to you.
There is something deeply satisfying about reproducibility.
Excellent. Now we may proceed.
I recommend confessing before I begin taking measurements.
random: Please do not touch the radium.
No, seriously. Do not touch the radium.
It glows beautifully in the dark.
We considered the glow quite convenient.
In retrospect, perhaps less handling would have been prudent.
My notebooks are perfectly safe. Provided you do not open them.
Apparently my notebooks require special storage now.
The laboratory had very poor ventilation.
Safety standards have improved considerably since my day.
What is this 'lead apron' everyone keeps mentioning?
I used to carry samples in my pockets.
Yes, these pockets.
Please stop backing away from me.
It is only a small amount.
The burns were an early clue.
Science occasionally provides feedback rather forcefully.
Pierre and I processed tonnes of pitchblende in a shed. Academia provided the shed.
Our laboratory was described as a cross between a stable and a potato cellar.
Funding has always been a scientific constant.
Radium is not green.
I don't care what the illustrators told you.
The blue glow is much prettier anyway.
I discovered two elements. One Nobel Prize seemed insufficient.
Fortunately, they eventually agreed.
Physics first. Chemistry later.
Two Nobels. Different sciences.
No, you may not borrow one.
I did not patent the radium isolation process.
Knowledge should be useful, not merely profitable.
During the war, I equipped mobile X-ray units.
I also learned to drive. The X-rays were easier.
There are few problems that cannot be improved by measurement.
There are several problems that can be made worse by radiation.
Please label your samples.
That is not glowing because it is magical.
Rasputin, step away from my equipment.
Crowley, this is chemistry, not alchemy.
Mr. Brahe, I appreciate the measurements. Please stop measuring my equipment.
Lady Lovelace is the only person here asking sensible questions.
I am surrounded by men who desperately need peer review.
Perhaps wash your hands.
Actually, definitely wash your hands.
We knew radiation was energetic. We were somewhat less clear on the consequences.
My definition of 'acceptable exposure' may be historically outdated.
secret_passage_entry: Interesting. Bring a light.
Before entering, I would like to measure the air.
An enclosed, poorly ventilated underground space. Wonderful.
Please do not lick the walls.
We should collect samples.
No one touch anything until I have examined it.
A hidden passage presents several excellent experimental opportunities.
If anything glows, call me before touching it.
If anything glows green, it probably isn't my fault.
This seems hazardous. I am interested.
Poor ventilation, unknown materials, no protective equipment. Familiar territory.
Proceed carefully. I have already exceeded several lifetimes of reasonable exposure.

start: Mary Mallon. Cook. And don't you start.
If anyone asks, I am perfectly healthy.
I've been locked up before. I didn't care for it then either.
Before anyone says anything: I feel fine.
They called me dangerous. I called them nuisances.
Right. Who's hungry?
I hope this place has a proper kitchen.
Nobody panic. That's how rumors start.
door_open: Finally. I was beginning to feel quarantined.
Good. I've had enough confinement for one lifetime.
About time somebody let me out.
See? Perfectly safe.
Open door. Fresh air. Sensible.
After you. Apparently people get nervous when I go first.
Excellent. Now, where's the kitchen?
They usually lock the doors behind me.
accuse: It's you. You've got a suspicious look about you.
I know when someone's hiding something.
You. And don't bother blaming me.
I've spent enough time being accused to recognize the guilty.
It's you. I can feel it in my perfectly healthy bones.
Everyone always looks at me first. This time, I'm looking at you.
I accuse you. How do you like it?
You've been acting strange. Stranger than the rest of us, anyway.
wrong_accusation: Well, now you know how it feels.
Fine. I was wrong. Apparently that's allowed when other people do it.
Perhaps we shouldn't lock anyone up without better evidence. Just a thought.
All right. You're innocent. Don't become smug.
Mistakes happen. Ask the New York Health Department.
So I accused the wrong person. Nobody died.
That proves nothing except that I was wrong once.
Fine. I'll wash my hands of the matter.
Apparently suspicion alone isn't evidence. Interesting.
correct_accusation: Ha! Not so pleasant being accused correctly, is it?
I knew it.
See? Sometimes the authorities get the right person.
Caught you.
And everyone thought I was the dangerous one.
Perhaps we should quarantine you.
Funny how evidence works when people actually have some.
There. Now leave me and my cooking alone.
I expect a written apology from everyone who doubted me.
random: I'm not sick.
Do I look sick to you?
I feel perfectly fine.
Nobody understands that part.
I cooked for dozens of families.
Some of them even stayed healthy.
Who's hungry?
I could make something.
Why did everyone stop eating?
It's only potato salad.
I make an excellent peach ice cream.
Why does everyone react like that when I mention dessert?
The ice cream had nothing to do with it.
Probably.
Wash my hands? Of course I wash my hands.
How many times?
You people have become very particular about hand washing.
Germs you cannot even see. Convenient accusation.
Apparently a person can carry a disease without being ill.
I remain skeptical.
They followed me for months.
Imagine being stalked because you're good at cooking.
They took samples.
So many samples.
I will not be discussing the samples.
North Brother Island was not my idea of a holiday.
Three years the first time.
Then they made me promise not to cook.
A ridiculous thing to ask a cook.
I may have returned to cooking.
Under another name.
That is not an admission.
Mary Brown is a very common name.
I needed work.
People get sick every day.
People got sick before I arrived too.
Usually.
Stop looking at my hands.
I said stop looking at my hands.
No, you cannot test my stool.
Absolutely not.
The doctors were obsessed with me.
Healthy woman, steady employment, suddenly everyone's a detective.
I don't trust bacteriologists.
They seem far too interested in other people's bodily functions.
Curie, tell them I look healthy.
Rasputin, you understand unreasonable doctors.
Crowley, whatever you're doing, keep it away from the soup.
Brahe, stop recording who ate what.
Lovelace, I don't care what the probability says.
Everyone here is afraid of me, yet Crowley is allowed to wander around unsupervised.
I have never poisoned anyone.
Infected is not the same word.
That came out wrong.
Perhaps I'll make sandwiches.
Why is everyone leaving?
secret_passage_entry: A secret way out? Now you're speaking my language.
I've escaped health inspectors before.
Does this come out beyond the quarantine fence?
Good. Nobody tell the Health Department.
I've had quite enough of locked rooms.
After you. If there's a kitchen, call me.
This reminds me of leaving jobs unexpectedly.
A hidden passage seems excessive. I usually just changed my name.
Excellent. Fresh employment opportunities.
If anyone asks, Mary Mallon never came through here.
Do you suppose this leads off the island?
Keep moving before somebody brings a bacteriologist.

enter: Enter. Quickly. Time is the one territory I cannot reconquer.
Ah. One of my more troublesome subjects.
Come in. Shut the door. I am running an institution, not a barn.
You have my attention. Do not squander it.
Another crisis? Excellent. I was becoming bored.
Approach. I have commanded armies less troublesome than this ward.
If this concerns Crowley again, be concise.
I have conquered nations with fewer interruptions.
Come in. And whatever Rasputin told you, ignore half of it.
Speak. I have paperwork multiplying faster than Austrians.
Yes, yes, come in. The empire apparently cannot govern itself.
State your business. Then leave me to mine.
accuse: You accuse them? Very well. Make your case.
An accusation is not evidence. Continue.
Interesting. And you are prepared to stand behind this?
Choose carefully. A commander who acts on poor intelligence loses more than arguments.
Very well. I shall hear the charge.
You suspect them. I hope your judgment exceeds your discretion.
Proceed. I enjoy decisive action when it is justified.
Names are easy. Evidence is harder.
You have accused one of my residents. Convince me.
I will permit the accusation. I make no promises regarding your dignity afterward.
Very well. Let us see whether you possess the instincts of a commander or merely the confidence of one.
incorrect_accusation: Your intelligence has failed you. Fortunately, no cavalry were involved.
Incorrect. Return when you have evidence rather than enthusiasm.
No. If this were a battlefield, your regiment would now be surrounded.
A disastrous assessment. I have invaded countries on better information.
Wrong. Even the Russians gave me more warning than this.
You have wasted my time and accused an innocent person. An impressive two-front failure.
Incorrect. Perhaps strategy is not your calling.
No. Go reconsider every decision that brought you to my office.
Wrong. I expected better. I frequently do. It is one of my weaknesses.
You have mistaken confidence for competence. A common disease.
Absolutely not. Were you hoping conviction would compensate for evidence?
Dismissed. Preferably before you develop another theory.
I have seen retreats conducted with greater dignity than this accusation.
No. And do not blame the weather.
correct_accusation: Correct. At last, competence.
Precisely. Decisive, accurate, effective. I approve.
You are correct. Perhaps there is hope for this institution.
Excellent. Good intelligence wins campaigns.
Correct. Have them brought to me.
Well done. Victory favors those who observe before they act.
You have identified the culprit. Efficiently enough.
Correct. I shall handle the rest.
At last, someone in this building understands reconnaissance.
Very good. I may promote you. There is nowhere to promote you to, but the sentiment remains.
Correct. France would have benefited from several more of you.
Excellent work. Do not become insufferable about it.
You were right. Enjoy the sensation; it is dangerously addictive.
Correct. A clean victory. Those are distressingly rare.
Well done. Now leave before I assign you administrative duties.
